rs-bd-conifer.back: Under or near conifers, with less visibility on the north and west sides.

rs-bd-eyes.front: How does a bedded deer cover itself?
rs-bd-eyes.back: Eyes cover below, nose covers behind and above.

rs-bd-approach.front: Best direction to approach a hillside bed?
rs-bd-approach.back: From the side or above, wind in your face. Not from below on a morning uphill thermal.

rs-bd-hot.front: Hot day: where do deer bed?
rs-bd-hot.back: Shade: conifers, north slopes, cool draws.
rs-bd-hot.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 310" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Where deer bed by weather. Hot sun: north slopes, shade and timber. Cold and clear: south slopes in the sun out of the wind. Windy: lee side and low draws. Rain or snow: under thick conifers. Deer pick beds for comfort.">

rs-bd-noon.front: Why not check beds at noon?
rs-bd-noon.back: Deer are in them. You evict them and teach them to move.

rs-bd-fawn.back: Not abandoned. The doe is close. Leave it.

rs-bd-snow.back: Old: icy refrozen bowl. Fresh: dry crisp floor.
